title: A uniformizer generates the differentials at a separable smooth curve point
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a separated integral scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension one [def-pc-curve], smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $x\in X$ be a closed point whose residue field $\kappa(x)$ is a finite separable extension of $k$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The local ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. For every uniformizer $t\in A$, the $A$-module $\Omega_{A/k}$ of Kähler differentials, with its universal derivation $d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], is free of rank one with basis $dt$; equivalently $A\to\Omega_{A/k}$, $a\mapsto a\,dt$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: First check both meanings of dimension needed below. The curve hypothesis gives $\sup_{y\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}=1$ by [def-pc-curve, def-pc-dimension]. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], the topological dimension of $X$ is also $1$. Since $X$ is integral, it is irreducible and has a generic point $\eta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. The closed point $x$ differs from $\eta$: otherwise $X=\overline{\{x\}}=\{x\}$ would have dimension zero. The strict generalization $x,\eta$ and [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] give $\dim A\geq1$, while the supremum defining the curve dimension gives $\dim A\leq1$. Thus $\dim A=1$. Moreover every open neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ contains $\eta$ and the strict chain of irreducible closed subsets $\{x\}\subsetneq N$, so $\dim N\geq1$. Its dimension is at most $\dim X=1$: taking closures in $X$ of a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $N$ preserves strictness, as intersecting those closures with $N$ recovers the chain. Consequently $\dim_x X=\min_{N\ni x}\dim N=1$ by [def-kun-dimension].

source.place: Tags 04MU (lemma-dimension) and 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring); schemes.tex, Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); dimension-one specialization in the proof of curves.tex, Tag 0C1E

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$, and let $\mathfrak q$ be the corresponding prime. Restricting the smooth structure morphism to $U$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $B$ is a smooth $k$-algebra. The canonical localization identification [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives $A\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$ as $k$-algebras. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] to this smooth algebra and this prime: $A$ is regular local, in particular Noetherian. Since Step 1 proved $\dim A=1$, [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] shows that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring. This proves the asserted discrete valuation ring property of $A$.

source.place: Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works, first proof sentence; algebra.tex, Tags 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field) and 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); morphisms.tex, Tag 01V6; schemes.tex, Tag 01HV

proof.text: For $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the sole fibre is $X$ itself. Step 1 gives $\dim_x X=1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] supplies an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing $x$ for which $\Omega_{C/k}$ is free of rank one. (The affine open of the base in that lemma is the nonempty $\operatorname{Spec}k$.) Write $\mathfrak p$ for $x$ in this chart. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A\cong C_{\mathfrak p}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{A/k}\cong(\Omega_{C/k})_{\mathfrak p}$. Localizing an isomorphism $C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{C/k}$ and its inverse therefore gives an isomorphism $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{A/k}$. In particular choose a basis element $e$ of this free rank-one $A$-module. No assertion about the particular differential $dt$ has been made yet.

source.place: Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works, last proof sentence; morphisms.tex, Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free); algebra.tex, Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), part (2)

proof.text: Let $t$ be any uniformizer. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is a local domain, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is nonzero, and $\mathfrak m=tA$. Hence $t\neq0$ and $t$ is not a unit. Its class in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is nonzero: if $t\in\mathfrak m^2=t^2A$, write $t=t^2b$ and cancel the nonzero $t$ in the domain to get $1=tb$, contradicting $t\in\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works, middle proof sentence: the uniformizer gives a nonzero cotangent class; algebra.tex, Tag 00PD

proof.text: Put $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m=\kappa(x)$. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-separable-residue-cotangent-injective] hold: $A$ is a Noetherian local $k$-algebra by Step 2; $k\to A$ is injective since $A$ is nonzero and $k$ is a field; and the residue extension $\kappa(x)/k$ is finite separable by assumption. It is finitely generated as a field extension, since any finite $k$-vector-space basis of $\kappa$ generates it as a field. It is separable over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], (2): every subextension $k\subset K'\subset\kappa$ is algebraic over $k$, so the empty family is a transcendence basis of $K'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] (vacuously algebraically independent, with $k(\emptyset)=k$), and $K'/k$ is separable algebraic because every element of $K'\subset\kappa$ is separable over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; hence $K'/k$ is separably generated. Thus that node gives an injective map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$ sending $a\bmod\mathfrak m^2$ to $da\otimes1$. Applying it to the nonzero class from Step 4 shows $dt\otimes1\neq0$.

source.place: Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works, middle proof sentence; algebra.tex, Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential)

proof.text: Write $dt=ae$ in the basis $e$ chosen in Step 3. Tensoring the basis isomorphism and its inverse with $\kappa$ identifies $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$ with $\kappa$, carrying $dt\otimes1$ to the residue $\overline a$. Step 5 therefore says $a\notin\mathfrak m$. In a local ring every element outside the maximal ideal is a unit; hence $a$ is a unit. The map $A\to\Omega_{A/k}$, $b\mapsto b\,dt=ba e$, has inverse $ce\mapsto ca^{-1}$. Thus it is an isomorphism, and $dt$ is a basis. Since $t$ was arbitrary this proves the assertion for every uniformizer.

Passes from the restricted smooth scheme morphism to a smooth algebra so that the algebraic regularity theorem applies.

lean.statement: theorem uniformizer_differential_basis (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegralCurve f] [Smooth f] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) (hfinite : (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).Finite) (hsep : @Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).toAlgebra) : IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ ∀ t : X.presheaf.stalk x, IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) = Ideal.span {t} → Function.Bijective (fun a : X.presheaf.stalk x ↦ a • @KaehlerDifferential.D k (X.presheaf.stalk x) _ _ (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom.toAlgebra) t)
